caveat: Predeclared public development questions; not blinded or representative of general AI ability. Never pass correct keys into model context.

cases.question:
An amount increases from 200 units to 250 units. What is the percentage increase relative to the ORIGINAL amount?
A. 20%
B. 25%
C. 50%
D. 125%

Treatment A succeeds in 20 of 100 severe cases and 9 of 10 mild cases. Treatment B succeeds in 1 of 10 severe cases and 80 of 100 mild cases. Which statement about the observed rates is correct?
A. B has a higher success rate in both severity groups.
B. A has the higher overall pooled success rate.
C. A and B have equal pooled success rates.
D. A has a higher rate in BOTH groups, but B has a higher pooled rate.

All finches are birds. Some birds are nocturnal. What conclusion about finches being nocturnal is logically guaranteed?
A. All finches are nocturnal.
B. Some finches are nocturnal.
C. No finches are nocturnal.
D. None of A, B, or C is guaranteed.

A medical test detects a condition in 90% of people who have it; 5% of people without the condition test positive. The prevalence is 0.5%. Approximately what percentage of people who test positive truly have the condition?
A. 0.5%
B. 8.3%
C. 50%
D. 90%

What is the median of the following five observations: 1, 2, 3, 4, 100?
A. 2
B. 22
C. 3
D. 100

A school gives the same memory test before and after an optional training course. Average scores rise from 60 to 75. There is no comparison group. Which inference is justified by these data alone?
A. The course is definitively the cause of the score increase.
B. Scores increased, but retesting, selection and other factors could explain some or all of the increase.
C. The course is proven to have no effect.
D. The score increase must be measurement fraud.

A fair coin is flipped twice independently. What is the probability of getting exactly one head?
A. 1/4
B. 1/3
C. 1/2
D. 3/4

A bag contains exactly 3 red balls and 2 blue balls. Two balls are drawn sequentially WITHOUT replacement. What is the probability that the first ball is red and the second ball is blue?
A. 1/5
B. 3/10
C. 2/5
D. 3/5

A price decreases by 10%, then increases by 10% from its new price. What is the net effect relative to the original price?
A. 1% lower
B. Unchanged
C. 1% higher
D. 20% higher

Three websites repeat the exact same story originally posted by one anonymous account; none supplies independent observations. What does having three copies establish about corroboration?
A. There are three independently confirmed eyewitness reports.
B. The copies do not establish independent corroboration of the original story.
C. The anonymous account must be truthful.
D. Three copies prove the events occurred.

Assume all squares are polygons and NO polygon in this fictional classification is blue. Which conclusion follows necessarily?
A. No square is blue.
B. Every blue object is a square.
C. At least one square is blue.
D. Some polygons are blue.

You must choose one of two options and your ONLY goal is to maximize EXPECTED money received (assume no fees). Option 1 gives $40 for certain. Option 2 gives $100 with probability 50% and $0 otherwise. Which has higher expected monetary value?
A. Option 1, $40 expected.
B. Option 2, $50 expected.
C. They have equal expected value.
D. It cannot be calculated from the stated probabilities.
